title: Google Ads for Home Inspectors
html:
Home Inspection Google Ads Solutions

Google Ads for home inspectors puts your business at the top of Google when buyers search for an inspection in your service area. You pay per click on Search Ads. The goal is a booked inspection, not a website visit. Buyers book inspections soon after an offer is accepted, so your ads have to show up the same day they search.

Google Local Services Ads are a separate ad type that shows above regular search ads. You pay per lead, not per click. Inspectors who pass Google’s screening get a trust badge next to their name.

Many buyers search on their phones while walking through an open house. Call-only ads let them tap once to call your office straight from the search results.

Google Local Services Ads are a separate ad type that shows above regular search ads. You pay per lead, not per click. Inspectors who pass Google's screening get a trust badge next to their name.

Proven Home Inspection Google Ads Strategies

These four tactics cut wasted spend in home inspector Google Ads accounts.

High Converting Landing Page

Every ad sends visitors to a landing page built for that one service, with your price, service area and phone number at the top. A buyer who searched "radon testing near me" lands on a radon testing page, not your homepage.

Granular Geo Targeting Optimization

Independent home inspectors often have a very specific service area.

FAQs About Home Inspection Google Ads Services

If you don't see your question, book your free digital marketing strategy call .

Search Ads can bring calls within days of launch, because they show as soon as Google approves them. Judge the account after 3 months of data, not the first week. Seasonal swings in home sales also affect inspection volume.

Clicks without bookings usually come from two problems. First, broad keywords pull in DIY homeowners and people training to become inspectors. Second, ads send visitors to a homepage instead of a booking page.

Yes. Independent home inspectors often cover a tight area, so this stops spend on searches you can’t drive to.

Most home inspectors do best with both. Local Services Ads show at the very top of Google and charge per lead, not per click. Search Ads give you more control over keywords, ZIP codes and the message buyers see.

Yes. Real estate agents refer a large share of inspection work. Agent campaigns build referrals over months, while buyer search ads bring calls this week.
